Alien: Isolation is an all around solid and fun experiance.
The stories plot takes place between the first two Alien movies where YOU, Ellen's daughter Amanda, try to uncover the mystery behind your mother's disaperance. You "arrive" at Sevastopol (a trading station that's already screwed before you get there from lost funding) to find the "rumored" flight recorder that belonged to the ship your mom was on, hoping it to shed some light on what the hell happened...
I was super impressed with how the Alien actually respondes to your play style and learns from it throughout the game. It constantly forces you out of your comfort zone, changing whatever strategy that worked previously, now obsolete. This means you are always on edge and thinking about the best way to deal with situations when face to face with the Alien.
**SPOILERS** you wont have very long to think...
The developers tell you on the difficulty selection to choose "Hard" for the real experiance, and so I did and looked back with no ragrets; If you're actually reading this and debating on playing the game, you should too!

Detail, detail, detail. It has been a few years since I have played one of the F1 series and this is by far the best one to date. The crazy levels of detail that the developers have included is insane - I noticed when racing in Singapore in the we that the rain is beutifuly detailed with colour from the lights AND the rain drops breifly stopped forming on my view as I went through that short covered section. That little detail which anyone could miss made me write this review.
So far 2/3 the way through my first season and I am really loving it.

I think this is probably the best F1 game yet. The driving characteristics are very good. There are definitely some issues with bugs though. This game crashes mid race for me all the time. I just finished singapore in career and it crashed ... Which means I have to do it all 31 laps again. Infuriating. The safety car is really buggy and causes you to get random penalties. I accumulated 3 Drive through penalties in one SC because it thought I passed people illegally and it thought I was too far away from the next car.
The Driving assists are excellent. The difference in difficulty between ABS and TC on and off is huge. The racing line is excellent, aside for some rainy conditions with worn tires that i've noticed. Both of these things make the game easy to get into but incredibly difficult to master. The AI is very good, though, I would definitely say they are inconsistent though. At level 70 - 80, I can easily catch them on most tracks. But on the difficult tracks like Monaco, they are insanely fast.

If you're an F1 fan, get this game. Career mode is immersive and fun. This year's rendition is much more friendly to the controller, i play on a controller and have no issues with tyre wear tests, like in previous titles.
Frequent patches have made AI seriously competitive, and they will race you in corners. First lap is still a mess though, and if you're dead set on divebombing, you can gain ridiculous amounts of positions to the first corner.
Slider difficulty is the greatest. Addition. EVER. You can customize your difficulty very precisely, being competitive with your teammate, but having no chance against the Mercs or Ferraris (As, unfortunately in the current year, is quite realistic.)
VSC and SC are quite buggy, and you might have a situation where under VSC conditions, car behind overtakes you and get to keep their position. Changing conditions are also quite weird, sometimes in qualifying, it rains for the first half of the session, the stops towards the end. The AI suddenly go from driving on a damp track, to a completely dry track,  while you will still drive on a damp track, giving you absolutely no chance against them.
TL;DR more features, difficulty SLIDER, controller friendly, immersive. Some bugs hopefully being fixed with frequent patches. To F1 fans, i highly recommend.

Transistor must be one of my favorite games. Upon launching the game, it strikes with its elegance and polish. As an example, the games goes the unconvetional path of omitting the use of a menu, a great idea, as it lets you get right into the action. Especially the level of animation underlines this elegance. But the real shine of the game is the combat system which presents a great amount of customizability. Notably the pace of a fight is refreshing since the game devides action into a relaxing planning phase and a hectic realtime phase. Another important aspect is the replayability the game offers through a mode called recursion (which I think is what the game is mostly about) and the difficulty customization the user has through so-called limiters, which, in my opinion, is the best way to solve the problem of creating difficulty levels in a game. As was the case with Bastion, the sound tracks in this game always hit, quite literally, the right note.

isometric action rpg with a highly configurable sword as your weapon. collect attacks as you progress.
you don't have to deal with a title screen menu
hold tab to hum to the music
you can pause time by entering turn mode and queue up a bunch of attacks
during turn mode the game displays predicted results of each move you make. (prediction is a bit odd, pushing enemies away might make you miss a subsequent short range attack)
alt-tabbing out of the game switches sound to some ambient sound rather than going silent
all UI elements and in-world details and turn mode overlays, including battle borders have a lot of neat animations going on
lots of lore to unlock and read
in-world designs includes painted imagery of electronic components and PCB without making it garish like games from the 90s
has a newgame+ mode that can be repeated many times without resetting your character stats. all battles are scaled appropriately

Pros: In Transistor, Supergiant Games has achieved a really interesting marriage between the action RPG and strategy genres. An engaging combat system will draw you in as it's and amazing soundtrack and gorgeous visual design make exploring it's tech-noir mystery storyline a pleasant and unforgettable experience. Definitely worth the price tag, specially if it's on sale.
Cons: Combat is an interesting new feature with a distinctive feel to it, but as it is usually the case in these kind of games, it will not be fully fleshed out unless you play in the harder "new game+" version of the game.
The story can get a little too poetical and abstract at times, making you feel like "Ok, sure, let's just keep going" more than "I wonder what that really represents" for some sections of the game.
All in all, pretty good game. Voice acting is great, even when you just hum to the music.

Plantera is a cute pixel graphic iteration of the popular clicker/idle game genres. If you have experience from the hardcore games of the genre, Plantera will feel shallow, empty and very very short.
However, those are the positives of this clicker. It is more like a relaxation tool than a 'keep clicking until your mouse and/or finger breaks' clicker. There isn't a lot to do: just plant some plants and add some animals, make a couple of clicks to get things started and then... Just watch, click whenever or collect the achievements in order.
So, if you are looking for something cute and easy to relax with, Plantera might be your thing. If you're looking something complicated and time-consuming, this won't please you.

My only criticism, after about 35h played, is that the world generator is a bit sloppy. You can adjust the random generation, but it's badly explained, and the actual world creation is too variable and general in its RNG. I.e. I think they could've done a much better job with the "generation rules", to converge all map generation to a similar starting point result. Many "default-amount" maps (medium amounts of everything) are literally unplayable because you're stuck on an island, resources are too scarce or enemies spawn too close (so you'll get attacked a bit too early).
Thankfully, restarting the game will randomize a new world in seconds and, if you do this maybe 10-15 times at most, you'll eventually find a suitable location.
So, what's the game itself like? Well, this is THE factory game out there. Incredibly deep with things to research and build. Also, being a manufacturing game, the game is an interesting puzzle when it comes to automating the construction of components like these massive mutli-step Rube Goldberg machines.
The game is really addictive, there's tons to discover, tweak and improve (without having a too steep learning curve) and it's super fun if you love building things and to figure out how to optimize things etc.
I'm absolutely recommending this game. Verdict - 9/10

You might not believe it but Paper Please is one of the best game I have played. Let me tell you why.
In the game you are a dude that has been assigned a job at the border. Your task is to check the people going in your country, and see whether or not their papers are in order. Simple enough eh? Yeah, that's what I thought at first too.
The first day you will have to check passports only. Yeah, check the dude's face, see if matches the photo in the passport, check if the date of birth is valid and stuff like that.
It will take time for you to check stuff and make sure you did not miss anything. And here is the whole game challenge:
. You see, every dude you process gives you money. If you take too much time analyzing papers you will process less people so you get less money.
At the end of the day you have to pay for the rent, for food and heat. Yeah, there is that side of the game too. Your child might get a cold so you will have to buy medecine. It costs a lot. So much that you will have to switch between a day with food and a day without, but with the heaters on. Sad but true.
The game goes very deep in the story;
. Between your family life that shows how poor your country is, you will read the newspaper at the beginning of the day. It gives mandatory information like which country is at war (so that means immigrants leaving that said country) and criminals that are unnacounted for (they could show up at your booth... eh who knows right?)
The more you progress in the game, the more papers you will have to check. First passport then work permit. Yeah too many immigrants are "stealing our jobs" so the government tells you to check work permits too now. Oh but some countries don't need those, but just a coupon instead. Yeah, we also forgot diplomatic papers and vaccination crap. Oh, this country refuses to import our goods? Today we'll teach 'em a lesson: do not accept work permit from THIS country only. Oh yeah? Some people are trying to smuggle shït? Here, now you get a scanner. Check for weapons and drugs. Don't miss anything.
"Hmmm sir, it is written here you are a woman...?"
"Yes I am, as you can see."
"Uh, ok, please step into the scanner please."
[Bzzzzz] Scanner picture shows tïts and püssy.
"Okay, si-I mean ma'am, all your papers are in order, have a good day."
"Thank you."
True story. However this scanner stuff takes TIME. So during this process you will quickly take the habit to process other papers. Yeah optimization man, I gotta feed my family man.
.
To feed your family you will have to sometimes skip checks. Sometimes you will genuinely forget to check something, like is there day 31 in February...? Uhoh. You have a blame if you let someone in with wrong/forged papers, or if simply there was something weird but you did not ask the dude for precisions.
Looking at that dude walking in the country, not being sure you checked everything. You feel like you missed something but you don't know what... dude is still walking... and... he passes. No warning, no blame. Looks like he was legit afterall. [Breath of relief]
Too many warnings and you will have money penalty. Less money for your family. They will get sick, starve and die. Think about your kid, his birthday is coming very soon. You would like to buy him a present yeah? Then you gotta work faster. Stop looking into your help book if said city is really part of that country: learn it by heart. This game can be a chore, it can be flat out boring and at times even feels like performing a real job.
And I absolutely ♥♥♥♥ing love it.
Papers, Please achieves what it strives to accomplish flawlessly, it haves you deal with choice, morals and monotonist work with the anxiety of the real struggle of providing for a family. The game sits you at the seat of a checkpoint for the fictional country of Arstotzka where you must asses people and decide whether they will be accepted entry into your country or denied based on a set of ever changing rules and guidlines. Once you open the checkpoint each day you are put on a timer, when this timer is finished the day will be over and you will be rewarded for every person you correctly assesed or penalized for each person who wrongfully accepted or denied entry. You will also be given a screen displaying your family including your wife, son, daughter and mother-in-law (as well as the possiblity of others depending on the path of your story) as well as their independent status' your financial screen which will show your savings, wages, rent and if you are low on funds you will decide whether you wish to buy heat for your appartment or food for your family as well as optional upgrades to your booth which are essentialy hot keys.
Throughout the game you will be given moral choices as to who you accept or deny as an example fairly early on the game (around day 4 or 5) a man is trying to escape a country with his wife as due to some sort of political issues they will be excuted similar to that of prejudices during WWII, his passport checks out fine so you let him through and his wife follows suit however her information is improper so now you may either accept her into the country and be penalized for it or deny her and let her die wrongfully and alone. While some may ignore these choices as neither of these characters are heard from again further in the story you will be given much larger choices which will impact the story, the way your checkpoint is run and even your family.
On the subject of your family they are one of the few short comings of this game, while you need to pay rent (if you are unable to pay rent the game will end) your own well being is not dependent on food or heat, this is simply to provide for your family. Your family is never actually seen nor is there any sort of interaction or dialogue between them and yourself, they are simply a status screen at the end of the day and you are not given any reason to care about them other than "they're your family".
As I said at the begining the game can be boring and at times will be hard to find enjoyment in actually playing but that's part of this games beauty, it manages to have you feeling like you're performing menial work and as if you truly are just trying to get by but there's something about it that just keeps you going and wanting to continue. However on that note I would reccomend playing the game in sessions as I found myself getting tired after long sittings with the game and ended up messing up more often, once again much like being exhausted with real work.
While I may not agree that this game is "art" as some may call it I will say that the game is a beautiful piece and a powerful statement on many aspects of politics and human nature. That all being said I highly reccomend this game and encourage you to play it.

I fondly remember playing this game with friends, and our descent from it 1 by 1 as it did so itself, in quality. This review will be a compilation of those feelings, but if you do pick up the game and enjoy it, all power to you.
The good
-3rd person: This is the best thing the game has going for it, and it's source of originality and allure as a MOBA. The third person aspect encourages skill shot abilities and dash/leap skills, this makes flanks, team fights, kills, and PvP combat in general more intense than the traditional top down aspect.
-Theme: The cast of characters in the game feature the wide array of gods from all the different pantheons of the world, their mythos tying into their abilities, where the devs attempted to make them all with diverse playstyles although the character models go from good to panderingly exotic.
-Miscellaneous: SMITE has multiple, different ranging game modes, fulfilling most player's niche of time constraints or challenges, the client is polished, and the game's asthetic looks modern and appealing in general.
The bad:
-Meta base and balance: Even in casual, almost half the gods in the game are rendered unplayable due to just how strictly and blatantly better they're alternatives can be. A forced meta of certain characters would be acceptable in say, merely ranked, if not for the fact that it is very much so apparent in casual games, where even in such an enviroment a lot of some of the characters are never played or worked over, making a stark amount of gods with very low play rates, much less people endeavoring to get good at them. This makes the game bland, when you play the same gods just to not get your♥♥♥♥♥kicked; which leads me to my next point.
-Player matchups: Although ranked provided decent matchups for the most part, casual is most certaintly a whole different story. Its quite simple: You get curbstomped or you steamroll, unless you break the algorithm and persuade your mates to play their best characters. While there are certain exceptions, the last few dozen casual games I played before falling out reflected the whole wreck or be wrecked doctrine that I endured.
-War of the glasscannons: SMITE is a game of powerful abilities and squishy characters. Also a deviation from traditional Mobas is how the game engages with abilities. The gods can be simply way too strong with too little health, and this is amplified with the lack of diversity in item builds which either go full damage or full defense (with the exception of bruisers), which late game doesn't even stand up to the damage without their CC. This makes the whole flow of the game follow through the with the previous point. Early game you throw, or get thrown out of lane very quickly, mid-to late game when people get into their kits and skills, anyone who gets the drop on you with an ounce of hard CC, (and you're not a bruiser or tank), and there is a lot, you will die. Another tie in with the potentially ludicrous ability damage can drop off the skill ceiling of the game, late game as some gods merely demands a sequence of mildly tedious button presses get immedeate kills.
-Irrelevance of towers and minions: Due to the high damage and low health, the devs probably thought it would be a good idea to make the minions and towers do minimal damage, making wave clears easy and non vital. By mid-game, an un-coordianated team dive can kill you, with inconsequential damage from the tower meant to protect you.
The Ugly:
Here I'll steer further from observational objectivity and into what I plainly see.
-Hi Rez and SMITE management: Its my belief that Hi-Rez is one of the laziest companies in the game industry as of now (I'm looking at you, paladins), and the changes and balances to the game show. Whenever there was an over-zealotized call from the community to nerf or buff a character/item, the developers respond in full, nerfing items and characters into the ground, making them unplayable and instilling the meta playstyle of the remaining "op" gods, avoiding significant nerfs.
-After playing this game for a while, I can admit to say that I did have fun, but the game itself, in my eyes, has become inherintly flawed and is now used by Hi-Rez, being their cornerstone product, to make money and has now lacked the careful developement and vision they may have had for it in the beginning.

Connected to the brand does it a disservice because you'll be expecting some form of quality that Dark Descent brought to the table. If you have played the first one, this one will come as a bit of a dissapointment. While the theme and the story are great, they have hindered many of the original game's key features.
1. You have no inventory. You no longer need to scavenge and explore to find tinderboxes, oil for your lantern (now electric), or any of the items you need to progress. This was one of the best parts of the first Amnesia. There was a sense of helplessness and vulnerability when you had to find all of the parts to make a potion or to fix a machine while your lamp was running out. This game is incredibly dumbed down.
2. Notes aren't voice acted anymore. Not that big of a deal, I know, but I really enjoyed all the extra effort that was prevalent in the first one when Daniel would read the notes to you, which made him seem more alive.
3. The game just isn't that scary. Probably the biggest dissapointment of all. The monsters in the trailer and teaser for the game made them look terrifying. In reality, all they are are pigs that freak out and walk quickly towards you, and they are easy to lose. And there aren't even that many! The creepy and eerie factor that the story brought you is there, minus the jump scares.
I really hope that they make a third that will really quench my thirst for the horror series, but for now, I think I'll stick with the first one.
Although this one was very short....it was still a heart stopping experience.

If you're looking for a terryfing survival horror game, this might not be your best choice. The pigs aren't very scary, and the times they appear and really become a threat to you is low.
But if you are looking for a game without jumpscares at every corner, but with a deep atmosphere, fascinating, cryptic storyline and beautiful soundtracks, then it is really worth the money. The game will really close you in, and throw you into a strange world, with an endless amount of machine rooms and dark secrets. The more you play it, the more you will want to know what happend to Oswald Mandus and his family.
Think about what you want, and then decide. If you want a second Dark Descent, i would'nt recommend it. But if you want a dark, atmospheric game with a bizzare story, this is your best choice!

The Dark Souls series has always been hailed as this super difficult game full of tough enemies and impossible bosses, when really it's not as hard as you would think. Do not let this false media image of the game intimidate you from playing this game. People complain about it being hard because they don't take the time to learn the game and how you're supposed to play it. It's not Call of Duty where you can rush into a room and quickscope everyone inside, nor is it The Force Unleashed with super duper combos and droves of enemies. You have to have skill and patience to be successfull at this game. After a couple hours in the game you will soon get the hang of it. With every new character I've created in the game I've experienced a huge learning curve because of how under-powered you are when you first start the game.
If you are wondering whether to buy this or Scholar of the First Sin, Scholar is the first game I've ever refunded on Steam. Scholar offers nothing special. You cannot play online with anyone from the original Dark Souls II on Scholar, which is a huge cockblock if your friends have DSII and you have Scholar. Scholar promises a "brand new Dark Souls II experience" when really it's the same♥♥♥♥♥♥put in different areas. Some bosses are now totally optional, such as the Belfry Gargoyles boss being entirely useless as the key to the area you need to fight the boss there is put before the boss instead of after the boss.
Don't think about purchasing Dark Souls II differently because people say it's "frustrating" or is full of "artificial difficulty." These are attention-seeking dumb♥♥♥♥s who hardly know what they're talking about. I've never had to retry a boss more than thrice, and I'm widely considered by everyone on my Youtube channel as a sucky player. This is one of the best games I've ever played and it's a shame people would turn away from an experience such as this because they fear they'll be gangbanged by mobs and crushed by bosses. Don't get me wrong, the game is no cake-walk. YOU WILL DIE. But the consequence of death only makes you feel more vunerable to the world around you. Games like Shadow of Mordor and Skyrim are nowhere near Dark Souls II when it comes to challenge. In those games you can clear a dungeon or kill a giant in no time at all with magical abilities and stomp the hell out of anyone who gets in your way. In Dark Souls II however,  you can't leasurely stroll through a dungeon and come out unscathed. Your health doesn't regenerate and you can't pause the game to spam a potion to revive yourself back to full HP in the game's real-time. You have to take every enemy as viable threat. Everything can kill you. Take it slow, and praise the sun.

TOBII 4C EYE TRACKING MINI REVIEW SERIES - F1 2017
CORE GAME SCORE 4/5
EYE TRACKING SCORE 4/5
(NB - I'm not reviewing the whole game, just how well the eye tracking worked FOR ME with Tobii 4C eye tracker e.g. was it well implemnted and did using it add something to the game. Assume if I'm bothering to review the game for it's implementation of eye tracking, I like the core game itself).
* Eye tracking is integrated into the game and settings are accessed via the game settings in game
* Eye tracking worked straight away.
* Look around 'extended view' worked well at default settings,  fairly smooth and well judged limits (though I tweaked it further to reduce the view).
* Looking at the bends as I turned and the screen view following my eye line view actually seemed to help me judge the racing line better and did add to immersion.
* Clean UI worked well and did dim distracting info HUD but was quick to reappear when I glanced in the right place on screen
* Although not officially supported, eye trackign on triple monitor worked ok for these features - accuracy at extremes (left and right) was poor but OK up to 1/2 way across the 2 auxillary monitors - VERY immersive combo as game allows you to limited HUD to centre monitor and EYE tracker makes it dim unless glanced at - side monitors give you peripheral vision for cars coming up on the sides, eye tracking helps you follow the road ahead and keeps distractions low, slight movement of screen as you drive added to immersion!
* (game also has good wheel support for G920 as well, adding to my simulator like immersion levels)
Overall, it worked well and definitely was better for playing with Tobii tracker than without - a show case for how to do this by Codemasters

Have you read "The Mysterious Island" by Jules Verne? Have you ever imagined yourself in the place of brave travelers? Have you ever thought what would you do in their shoes to survive? I experienced this novel with its characters several times, and with Cyrus Smith improves the lives of unwitting colonists and built a new civilization away from the rest of the world. Now imagine that you are in a similar situation, and you can independently use their skills and abilities to help yourself out with the "mysterious island". How? Modern computer games allow you to check it for yourself. I accidentally found on the Internet site of the game “Factorio”. Imagine the distant future. You are the pilot of a spaceship that crashed on a distant planet. And you have to try to leave this planet from scratch building a mining and processing industries, creating assembly lines and research centers and in the end build a spaceship. But all is not as easy as it seems. The Resources are few, and the planet is inhabited and its inhabitants, dissatisfied with pollution caused by your production, begin to attack you and you need to defend yourself from their attacks.
The idea of ​​this game and the opportunity to relive childhood memories fascinated me and I enthusiastically cast aside all my current affairs and began to play! Although at first glance the game is not boring, but in the game there are situations related to the routine "work" and a manifested monotony. In the early stages this “dig-extractive-operation-researching” process turns into the “dig-extraction-system-researching” process but for the next level of development of science and technology. Stone furnace is replaced by the steel furnace and electric technology as the study and improvement of science, steam generators are replaced with solar panels on the coal is replaced with a crude oil and other forms of energy. But in the end you achieve the ultimate goal!
In general, the game has caused pleasant emotions in me and I feel it will remain in my library of games for a long time

A worthy sequel to Bastion. While the narrator in Bastion has been a tiny bit more engaging than your commentating companion in Transistor, the combat system more than makes up for it.
Choose on the fly between the classical real time combat system or a turn-based system, although you will probably use a hybrid of both depending on your enemies.
Your skills are introduced in a unique way with a nice personality attached to them and combining your abilities with each other is a lot of fun

Transistor is at once a better and worse game than Supergiant's first offering, Bastion. It has certain thematic inconsistencies and inexplicable plot holes, but at the same time offers an elevation of aesthetic design and represents the continued improvement of Darren Korb, who provides an even more excellent soundtrack with strong assistance from Ashley Barrett,
You play as Red, a woman whose voice (and so much more) have been stolen from her by a shadowy cabal that has unleashed an unstoppable force upon the idyllic cyberpunk utopia of Cloudbank. Can the Process be stopped? What even is it, and what is the Transistor, the mysterious sword she carries at her side?
It's not that you only learn fragmentary answers to any of these questions: it's regocnizing that any whole answer would only be a half-truth, incapable of capturing the vague, fleeting, ephemeral nature of this game's core. How frustratingly post-modern, I know--it's going to force you to think, recognize its inconsistencies, and accept that they are--to a degree--deliberate.
Come for the beautiful songs, and stay for the crazy-as-all-hell attack combinations you can build out of the funtions on your sword.

Well, I sure was hoping this would be worth the incredibly low price of $15... Which in reality, it would've been for the 10 or so hours I played it for the free weekend. To me, 10 hours of gameplay is definitely worth $15. But I've played that long now and the games flaws are too encumbersome to ignore.
The physics in this, if you have played Just Cause 2, are even worse. In fact, exponentially worse. Just Cause 2 had glaring flaws, like automatically going into a freefall for seemingly no reason and then causing you to die or take massive damage on a tiny impact. JC3 has sort of the opposite problem. You can fall from insane heights and not even take any damage at all.
The parachuting in this doesn't feel remotely realistic and trying to use the physics in your favour to gain momentum is unnaturally finnicky. JC2's grappler, parachuting and movement in general was so much better. You also actually had a melee attack, something severly lacking from JC3.
Driving is nearly impossible, something which isn't necessary for getting around the map. But you do need to drive in missions and challenges. I spent the first 8 hours or so just clearing the entire first region and finally started doing missions for the last couple hours. So I had to drive, fly, boat and traverse as much as possible because I was under the impression they also took out fast travel in this game. Come to find it's a random mission where you push a boat into water... I think the fourth mission? I didn't watch any cutscenes because the acting and story are really bad. But what does a boat have to do with giving me the ability for my crew to pick me up in a HELICOPTER to take me somewhere.
I could go on and on about how disappointing this game is in comparison to its predecessor... But I think I've said enough to at least get the point across. I hummed and hawed about buying this when it came out and good thing I waited. I would've been so incredibly angry to spend $70 or $80 on this...
I 100% completed Just Cause 2 on 360 and loved the game so much that I also bought it on Steam to play multiplayer and get all the dlc for a very cheap bundled cost. I probably put 300 - 400 hours into JC2 and I'm not even willing to put any more time into this frustrating mess...
I should clarify though that I did not really have any performance issues throughout the game. Like, none really at all except for one crash while I was flying a helicopter across the sky over the water. Aside from that, there's expected little dips of maybe 3 - 5fps when there's tons of objects on screen after/during explosions and many NPCs in the area. But I was actually impressed how well the game ran for how many issues there were elsewhere. And, for how much flora and how many destructible things are in the game.
Not recommended unless the game is free for another weekend really.. I'd pay $15 for the 10 - 15 hours of fun, but definitely do not buy extra stuff or spend more than $15 on this.

Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs is a controversial game. Some people hate it, while others adore it.
Amnesia: A Machine for Pigs was developed by thechineseroom, the same people who brought us Dear Esther. I'm personally not fond of Dear Esther myself, but that is for another review.
The gameplay is probably the biggest difference between the two games. In A Machine for Pigs, the game is much more linear than The Dark Descent. There are not many areas to explore, as most of the areas require you to finish the puzzle and continue your way on. Personally this did not bother me very much, however if you are a hardcore Amnesia fan this might upset you. The game has very few items to grab and fool around with; mostly items required for the path are the only items that can be grabbed. A Machine for Pigs removes the inventory, which automatically removes all aspects of obtainable items.
The monsters in A Machine for Pigs are much different from The Dark Descent in many ways. It is clear they are from a different type of horror, being The Dark Descent monsters much more scary. The ManPigs in A Machine for Pigs are not scary to the extent the monsters are in The Dark Descent; however some monsters later in the game might sway ones opinion. I will not go into detail of the monsters to reveal any spoilers.
Possibly the most obvious change from The Dark Descent is the setting. The Dark Descent took place during the 1800’s in a castle, while A Machine for Pigs takes place during the last hours of 1899 of London. All of the scenery is replaced with early 20th century buildings and machinery, with the end result looking spot on for the appropriate time frame.
A Machine for Pigs sadly is not very user friendly in the custom story department, as the game has no support for custom stories.  If you own The Dark Descent, you can head over to Frictional Games’ forum to obtain the pre-release of an upcoming update for The Dark Descent to utilize the new model format (.FBX) from A Machine for Pigs.
Overall opinion: A Machine for Pigs was scary, but not scary enough. That being said, the story is fantastic and much better than The Dark Descent in many ways. Without reading the notes, the player might become confused what happened in the story. If you are a fan of Amnesia and of pigs, this title is for you. If you didn’t find A Machine for Pigs scary, try The Dark Descent. If you think either one of those are not scary, try out the Penumbra series created by Frictional Games. Penumbra might change your opinion quickly.

TL;DR - A casual hunting simulator with a lot to offer if you're actually into this sort of thing. Not as difficult as people complain about, just a matter of using the wiki and learning from experiences. The option to pay is for people that REALLY want a hunting sim - it's a fairly niche genre that hasn't seen huge evolutions in pay models - this is my first non-buy2play and I'm into this sort of thing, for example.
This an enjoyable, casual hunting simulator with a satisfying gun experience. You can certainly have fun with the single gun and  single species (effectively; rabbits are now allowed, but you need to buy a shotgun - can be done with earned currency) they allow you to hunt for free. This is not a game that you play all day. This is a game that you  play for, maybe, an hour or two when you're up for it and want a casual experience. Animals will not walk into your path as you sprint through the forest - you actually have to hunt them - which I feel people that complain about this game just don't get. It's not a first person shooter with instant gratification. It offers progression, albeit slow, in the form of tracking, spotting, and weapon skills, as well as internal achievements to increase your (largely cosmetic) hunter score. Respectively, the skills allow for more accurate judgements of an animal's movement, increased accuracy in judging an animal's weight and score, and decreased weapon sway. Potentially a selling point, the game's developers are active and actually seem interested in the opinions and wellfare of their players. As for pricing, I think things are, for the most part, reasonably priced. Clothing may not seem worth it to everyone, but I find their bonuses effective and the items aesthetically pleasing. Weapons are mostly in the $5-$7 range, typically allowing for a scope purchase with a rifle, though you really only need a single extra scope (for the Anschutz rifles). $9.99 for 3 months (~$3/month) of free rein over the entire reserve and its animals, along with unlimited ammunition for the weapons you own, and tempting starter packs, is reasonable to me. I cannot speak on the graphical quality, because all of my settings are set to the lowest in order to see farther. Runs slick as silk on my stock Lenovo Y50.

"Oh, i guess they don't like to swim" as you pass by a pond. "Let me tell you a joke.. What's the difference between... You know what? nevermind" during a lift ride (loading screen disguised)
* The Combat. It is nice in the beggining but gets repetitive really fast. you do get some powers but they mostly play out the same. You fully heal between fights and can save everywhere. If you die, you don't really die as the time stops and you lose one of your attacks until the second next checkpoint. I really wish it had more depth, but in the end it was  1- stop time 2- queue some attacks 3- run as your time stop ability recharges 4- repeat
* The story. I am a little biased because i skipped all terminals. Or maybe i skipped them all because the reading doesnt really fit the action oriented gameplay. I didn't understand many points but in the end i didnt bother going after the information. I was just happy the game was ending. Also, I didn't care about the protagonist.
* The protagonist. Female silent protagonist. you are supposed to feel her emotions through her music (why is she a singer anyway?) and like her because of her appearance (red haired, nice body, etc). But you don't. She is shallow. Lacks personality. She just does what the sword tells her to do. The ending went against what was being shown, though.
* The length. It was quick. Surprisingly quick. When the final cutscene appeared i though I was just less than halfway though but it was actually the end. I was just level 11 and still had space for countless powers and upgrades. i didn't even unlock most restrictions.  What happened ?
* The linearity. I guess if they went a route a little more like bastion it would have been better. many stages that you get a new power per stage, or something like that. But this game just makes you follow the path and that is it.
I really loved the ending, though. But it doesn't make the game any better
I wish i liked it, but i really didn't.

Well, I sure was hoping this would be worth the incredibly low price of $15... Which in reality, it would've been for the 10 or so hours I played it for the free weekend. To me, 10 hours of gameplay is definitely worth $15. But I've played that long now and the games flaws are too encumbersome to ignore.
The physics in this, if you have played Just Cause 2, are even worse. In fact, exponentially worse. Just Cause 2 had glaring flaws, like automatically going into a freefall for seemingly no reason and then causing you to die or take massive damage on a tiny impact. JC3 has sort of the opposite problem. You can fall from insane heights and not even take any damage at all.
The parachuting in this doesn't feel remotely realistic and trying to use the physics in your favour to gain momentum is unnaturally finnicky. JC2's grappler, parachuting and movement in general was so much better. You also actually had a melee attack, something severly lacking from JC3.
Driving is nearly impossible, something which isn't necessary for getting around the map. But you do need to drive in missions and challenges. I spent the first 8 hours or so just clearing the entire first region and finally started doing missions for the last couple hours. So I had to drive, fly, boat and traverse as much as possible because I was under the impression they also took out fast travel in this game. Come to find it's a random mission where you push a boat into water... I think the fourth mission? I didn't watch any cutscenes because the acting and story are really bad. But what does a boat have to do with giving me the ability for my crew to pick me up in a HELICOPTER to take me somewhere.
I could go on and on about how disappointing this game is in comparison to its predecessor... But I think I've said enough to at least get the point across. I hummed and hawed about buying this when it came out and good thing I waited. I would've been so incredibly angry to spend $70 or $80 on this...
I 100% completed Just Cause 2 on 360 and loved the game so much that I also bought it on Steam to play multiplayer and get all the dlc for a very cheap bundled cost. I probably put 300 - 400 hours into JC2 and I'm not even willing to put any more time into this frustrating mess...
I should clarify though that I did not really have any performance issues throughout the game. Like, none really at all except for one crash while I was flying a helicopter across the sky over the water. Aside from that, there's expected little dips of maybe 3 - 5fps when there's tons of objects on screen after/during explosions and many NPCs in the area. But I was actually impressed how well the game ran for how many issues there were elsewhere. And, for how much flora and how many destructible things are in the game.
Not recommended unless the game is free for another weekend really.. I'd pay $15 for the 10 - 15 hours of fun, but definitely do not buy extra stuff or spend more than $15 on this.

I haven't played this game much, but so far I like it and would recommend it to others who are looking for something different. It's very much an indie game and it really is a "job simulator" or a "paperwork simulator" so you would think that it would be pretty boring. Well, as my teenage daughter said when watching my wife play, "it's sort of boring, but sort of interesting."
I think what makes the game interesting is the story of a working class man in a fictional communist country trying to make ends meet at his bureaucratic job that pays him peanuts. He's got his own problems to deal with keeping his family fed, warm, and healthy. BUt as he goes through the motions everyday of stamping passports, allowing or denying people at his checkpoint, he is confronted sometimes with other people's problems. What does he do? Does he just follow the rules of his employer/government and cover his own butt? Or does he sometimes break the rules when seemingly honest people might be in trouble and might need help from him? I think it's this tension that makes the game interesting. It's not always clear what is the right thing to do.
You have to have a quick eye and pay attention to details in this game since you can make a little more money the more people you proces each day. But if you make too many mistakes and break the rules, then your bosses penalize you. So you have a lot of incentive to be merciless to those who sometimes approach you for help. So the game sort of encourages you to be a cold-hearted bureacratic machine and makes it hard to do what you think is the right thing to help someone in need. I think that is part of the tension that makes the game good. You can let someone through who doesn't have the right paperwork and your bosses will give you a warning about that, and that puts pressure on you to not make any other followup mistakes or you'll lose some of the little money you make.
The pixelated, retro graphics that are in this game seem to be all the rage these days with indie games these days, and I honestly am getting tired of the trend, but in this case the visuals really work well because they enhance the bleakness of the setting of the game.
This is definitely a game to try out if you are looking for a different gaming experience, especially if you can get it on sale.

This is an excellent game and was my first Total War game in general. I bought it when it was on sale for 15$, and had I known I'd put almost 2000 hours into this, I'd have happily paid the full 60$. As most games at that price don't come close to the amount of entertainment and time I've received from this game.
Set in the early days as Rome was just becoming an empire and Greece was falling from grace and power, this game offers a wide diversity of factions to play as. Whether you favor the civilized Romans, the savage Barbarians (oh boy is there a lot of them), or one of the many Eastern empires, there's always something new to try. I've spent hundreds of hours building empires for the Spartans, British (Iceni), Romans, Egypt, and Armenia. And when I grew bored of that, there was a whole new challenge waiting for me in online battles and multiplayer campaigns.
Gameplay wise, it was easy enough to pick up and learn basic battle strategies, as I've never played a strategy game before this, and yet there was enormous room for challenging myself as I got better. The mod scene is amazing as well. Loads of support and variety to fine tune the game to your exact preferences. The follow up game to this, Total War Attila introduces a lot of new features that I wish had been introduced in this game, but alas this is still the better game in my opinion. Attila is very dark, and has a bland monotone map, and set in a time period which I have very little interest in. As best I tried to enjoy that game, it does not come close to this one.
Mind you, I picked up this game right as the Emperor Edition was released, and I have no idea or opinion on Rome 2's initial release. However, this game, as it is right now, is fantastic and definitely worth the money. Are there issues? Sure but every grievance I've had with the game was fixed by finding a mod to improve the AI, or adding new unit packs to less diverse factions, and so forth.
Amazing, yes this game gets a lot of grief, but in terms of fun and cost/hours played, you will definitely get your moneys worth.

Broforce is honestly one of the most entertaining games I've played in a long time. The premise is simple, but funny, and the atmosphere and action they set up only adds to the obscurity of this game. In short, you're in for one hell of a ride.
Pros:
This is a simple and easy-to-master game that makes most side-scroller shooters fun to play. The simplicity in graphics also makes this game ideal for computers that perform poorly or can't handle most triple A titles. The game and its controls are easily mastered, being that each character in the Broforce cast has a special set of abilities to be exploited in the frontlines. As I already made mention of, before, the game is designed for comical purposes and parodies popular action and thriller movies. This is complemented by the characters you can unlock - each named using the word "bro" somewhere in the title - allowing you to easily navigate through levels and fight hordes of under-educated, under-trained, terrorists that explode or splat into a viscera of digital blood. With all of this, the game is a great and well-made indie classic that I would suggest for anyone looking for a retro-styled game with good controls and easy-to-understand logic.
Cons:
This game is a lot of fun, but it is still an indie game, in that the difficulty of certain levels can vary widely. An example is when you first start to fight bosses on various levels, you'll experience little to no resistence with the regular forces. After ravaging the enemies and destroying half the level in the process, you'll suddenly experience a massive difficulty curve in fighting the boss character, whatever vehicle or enemy that may be, which may suck up your lives and time. This is by design and helps spice things up, however, so you may not find this as much of a problem as some do. The only biggest con that is a genuine pain is dealing with certain boss battles in relation to level-destructibility. All of the levels can be completely decimated, which is super fun to do, but this presents a nasty issue, when it comes to trying to traverse certain terrain, or get to a boss. This becomes especially apparent when dealing with enemies that can shoot artillery shells and what not, which may unintentionally cause you to fall to your death.
All of this makes a great and funny game that is easy to enjoy and very light-hearted, at the same time. A definite win, in my book, anyways.

Very good career mode. I didnt play 2016 so cant compare to that but it makes you feel like you are part of the team. You have to earn points and spend those points on the area of the car that you want/need to develop, almost like a skill tree in an RPG. The points are earned by performing certain tasks during practice and for good performance during the qhole weekend.
The driving physics are really nice. Of course non of us have driven an F1 car but if you follow F1 you will know about the torque of the current engine and how to have to be carefull with the throttle so you dont light up the rear tyres etc.
The game looks great and I get a very good steady frame rate, but every two or 3 races i might get a slight frame drop which would be mildly annoying but usually doesnt affect my laptimes.
The whole classic car thing isnt for me, it was fun the first couple of times but now it just feels like a chore so i just skip them, but you can definatly feel the difference in the amount of torque, grip and overall performace there is between cars from just a few years ago to the current generation.
I play with a racing wheel which feels fantastic, i havent tryed playing with a controller but i dont think the experiance would be anywhere near as great, although its not a full sim racer and it is available on console so i would expect you can fiddle with the settings and it would be just fine with a controller.
It is realistic in the sense than teams like McLaren are massively down on power so if you race for them expect to have a tough season to start with, but that is all part of the experience.
If you are an F1 fan with a wheel i would say this is a smart purchase. If you are not and F1 fan then why are you reading this review? :D:D:D

Game music is awesome - tutorial definintely beneficial to follow. Story overall is interesting- and voice over for important characters in conversation as well as the party themselves is fantastic- well done and at times a bit humourous. Some of the misspellings in the introductions as well as tutorials I believe need to be looked into and fixed as there seems to be a few words here and there in all of the descriptions  I read.
Game crashed one time only - so not a bad thing. There is no controller support - however you are able to WASD but in order to do so you have to RT click on your mouse outside of anything you can interact with - and then your character can move. This is not in the tutorial - and unfortunately not many other PC games that I play have the character locked down. So I missed speaking the tavern group in the first city I was in - not a total crapper but unsure of what they may have had to tell me that may have been important. Finding my way back was a bit dicey until I got used to the map - also not in the tutorial.
Aside from the above I was still intrigued by the game and enjoyed it. It's simple in the makings of it but hard when you attempt to strategize how you're going to take on an enemy - or who to stand watch for days on end; the fact that I couldn't find the specific herbs to cure one of my party members - I just kept casting the BALM spell to keep her healthy for the timebeing. It's great and I enjoyed it and will continue my quest as I only had the one and still played it for 4 hours just exploring what my character can do- and where to find clothes and reading the tutorials that popped up from place to place to help guide you through.
You can also make up your own diary and make notes about where you've been what you found there on the map just in case you need to travel back to that location for anything.
Definitely a lot to do in the game.

Rome 2's reputation was severely tarnished by a number of bugs when the game was first released.  Fortunately these have now been mostly resolved and I can say that this is one of the best Total War releases I've ever played.  If you've ever played a Total War game, you'll know the drill by now - take control of a historical faction and conquer the♥♥♥♥♥♥out of everything.  Rome 2 is a little different though, in that you now have different types of victories (military, economic and cultural).  For example, achieving an economic victory will require you to have a set amount of cash in addition to holding a set number of provinces.  I say provinces, not cities, as this is another addition to the franchise.  Each province consists of a number of settlements, but only one, the capital, has any substantial defences, such as a wall and towers.  In order to completely control a province, you must control all the settlements within it.  By controlling the whole thing, you will be able to issue edicts which gives your faction bonuses.  It's an interesting addition, and one which works.
The game still suffers from issues that have plagued the Total War franchise since the beginning, most notably a questionable AI that does strange things at times.
All in all though, it's a very good game and I highly recommend it.  And yes, it is better than Rome 1.

I haven't played this game much, but so far I like it and would recommend it to others who are looking for something different. It's very much an indie game and it really is a "job simulator" or a "paperwork simulator" so you would think that it would be pretty boring. Well, as my teenage daughter said when watching my wife play, "it's sort of boring, but sort of interesting."
I think what makes the game interesting is the story of a working class man in a fictional communist country trying to make ends meet at his bureaucratic job that pays him peanuts. He's got his own problems to deal with keeping his family fed, warm, and healthy. BUt as he goes through the motions everyday of stamping passports, allowing or denying people at his checkpoint, he is confronted sometimes with other people's problems. What does he do? Does he just follow the rules of his employer/government and cover his own butt? Or does he sometimes break the rules when seemingly honest people might be in trouble and might need help from him? I think it's this tension that makes the game interesting. It's not always clear what is the right thing to do.
You have to have a quick eye and pay attention to details in this game since you can make a little more money the more people you proces each day. But if you make too many mistakes and break the rules, then your bosses penalize you. So you have a lot of incentive to be merciless to those who sometimes approach you for help. So the game sort of encourages you to be a cold-hearted bureacratic machine and makes it hard to do what you think is the right thing to help someone in need. I think that is part of the tension that makes the game good. You can let someone through who doesn't have the right paperwork and your bosses will give you a warning about that, and that puts pressure on you to not make any other followup mistakes or you'll lose some of the little money you make.
The pixelated, retro graphics that are in this game seem to be all the rage these days with indie games these days, and I honestly am getting tired of the trend, but in this case the visuals really work well because they enhance the bleakness of the setting of the game.
This is definitely a game to try out if you are looking for a different gaming experience, especially if you can get it on sale.

Like the Chinese Room's Dear Esther, Amnesia: A Machine For Pigs seems more like an art project than a video game. Many of the game mechanics from The Dark Descent are gone, no inventory, sanity, or latern oil remain. There is very little survival or horror in this sequal to one of my favorite survival horror video games. If you expect this to be like the original then you will most likely be disappointed.
All of that being said, the game does look good - in an artistic way, this isn't CryEngine. The music fits the atmosphere very well, and the story isn't too bad either. If you pick this game up on sale, or you don't enter the game with too many expectations, then you will most likely enjoy it. It's not bad, but in my opinion Frictional Games messed up by having the Chinese Room develop this. I wish I could give a more neutral recommendation, but given the binary option Steam gives me I will have to say No, I will not recommend this game. This is mostly because I was personally disappointed, but you may not be - so don't let that stop you from playing.
I hope that there's another Amnesia game in the future, but I hope that next time Frictional Games goes back to how they made The Dark Descent.

It's one of those standard, generic Zombie survival games. However it's reasonably polished, and is genuinely fun to play.
The game is centered around realism, you have to check your ammo, there are no HUD elements consistently on-screen, you get diseased, so have to take pills to stave off (not cure) the infection.
At first it feels like a hit below the belt, but you'll soon find that the game about the hopeless struggle to fend off zombies shouldn't let you role-play as Rambo, or Superman. This is what a Zombie apocalypse would feel like if you were there in person.
The game is difficult, pi\unishing and combined with the superb soundtrack conveys an ubiquitous sense of despair. However as in Dark Souls, this sense is contrasted by the elation you experience when finally, after weeks of trying, you get to be on the winning team.
Also, there's no way of paying your way to victory: no microtransactions, no DLC with better guns and higher drop rate of supplies. The game has excellent Linux support, probably the best running game on my library.
Overall, if you are a hardcore survivalist, or you simply want a truly free game - this is for you.

Excellent. Easily the best Alien franchise game. Very good at accomplishing exactly what it sets out to do, which is create a tension filled cinematic stealth/survival horror experience in line with the final sequences of the first film. You're either not invested in the game or a teenager trying too hard to be cool if you don't think this game is terrifying when you play. The art and sound design are top notch and absolutely capture the retrofuture look from the first film scarily accurately and most of the cast from the original film even shows up for bits on some audio logs (and the story DLC, but pick those up on sale as they're very short, but sweet sequences). The story is even pretty neat, if a bit of an Alien franchise pastiche and so kind of predictable.
That said, it's not flawless. I ran into some audio bugs that would occasionally cut out sound including a pretty major scripting/audio bug that stopped a character from saying their lines throughout a puzzle sequence they were supposed to verbally guide you through. So I died like 9 times trying to figure out the instant-death puzzle by rote memory while being confused since the character was not providing context for what was going on. Still could just be my machine on that one.
The game also feels padded at times, a bit here and there in the first half, and more generally in the second half, and the collectibles are at direct odds with the tension of the game. There's never a great point to hunt them down, as the plot of the game pushes you relentlessly forward, and tons require backtracking to find. While the Nostromo logs are neat, the ID tags are lame and there are no rewards or anything for putting in the extra effort. Generally, cutting bits of the main game down probably would have led to an even better experience.
Biggest flaw though is a "good problem to have." In that this is a great game that demonstrates a developer who knows what they're doing and should recieve a sequel based on the exceedingly high quality of the product alone. But it's a game concept so fully explored that there's nothing for a sequel to possibly add, except tedium and redundancy. You just know Fox Interactive will want to milk the hell out of this, but it really should just be a one & done.
Still, absolutely excellent overall. Especially coming from a dev that's most known for grand strategy games, which is really random. Worth the time even if you don't like Alien much, though not for the faint of heart.

The last F1 game (from CodeMasters) that I purchased was F1 2012. I was dissapointed that progress towards making a more polished game was not happening so from F1 2013 until F1 2016 I did not support CodeMasters products. I decided that this year however I would give them another shot. The game, from the outside, looks much better and the handling of car physics has met that nice balance of sim versus arcade. It is still absolutely closer to the realm of arcade but it will most likely please even sim nuts who just want a purpose build F1 game.
However...I still see bugs and issues in the game that were present in F1 2012. First off, the safety car can still cause wrecks. The "please use multiple tire compounds" bug that will DSQ you even when you do use both compounds still happens in online races. Speaking of online races, have they made...ANY progress on making this experience better? No matter where your opponents live on this planet, you are going to get a super ♥♥♥♥♥♥ connection race. It is really hard to take it seriously when the other racing games on PC have miles upon miles of better experiences.
Looking at other PC racing games/sims, where in the hell is VR support? You had it in Dirt Rally and now you just abandon it? I get the the PC market is niche but look at almost every other PC racing game and what do you see? VR support.
If you are looking for a single player experience, then sure F1 2017 can scratch that itch. However it is still a buggy experience and without VR it feels like a bad value against other racing games on PC. I cannot recommend this game unless you do not have last year's version. If you have any previous version, stick with that.

AVOIDED THIS GAME BECAUSE OF MIX REVIEWS AND I REGRET THAT, SO DONT AVOID IT AND GIVE IT A TRY IF IT INTERESTS YOU! Ok First of all IGNORE all the negative reviews this game is getting. People complain about lag, bots (arent a big problem imo unless theyre one shotting mobs u need to farm for, u can always switch channels), the prices of there dlc, ect. I highly reccommend this game to anyone! Don't take the mi/negative reviews to seriously as its just people complaing about little things i havent even noticed. Then again im only level 61. Haven't came across bugs, except for just one and thats that my quest giver wasnt accepting my quest, even though i could teleport to him and the quest said it was done. It was just a side a side quest though so nothing major, and it only happened once. The Market limitations arent even that bad unless u want to sell more then one thing on the board, then i can see why u would complain, but tbh i never really use the market in mmos anyways. Only to buy minor things or things i need and thats it. The game is very fun and im glad i didnt avoid it, my friend was the one that reccomended me this game and im glad i jumped in and gave it a shot. Really fun! My only annoyance with the game is playing as Cleric cause i have to auto attack every ******* thing that flys cause my cure cant affect them on the ground and the damage u dish out is low to. while every dps class just one shots everything, ur sitting there like an idiot it trying to auto attack one to death. It can be a pain like certain placed that swarm with banshees and stuff. Now i highly recommend this game to anyone familiar with mmos because it really is fun, but get some friends to play with u or make some cause it can get lonely higher up in like around 55-60. Around that level (really my only con) you only find like a few people because in those areas you dont really stay there to long, Kind of lonley to lol. Anyways ill provide tips for new players down below.
Tips:
1. Start in Klaipeda, I notice more stuff drop there and it really is overall better. I started in Orsha and i didnt get as many equipment as i did their. Also, while in Klaipeda I also got monster cards which i didnt get in Orsha when i reached to Navaha.
2. You dont need to grind if you reach a brick wall! Go to the town u started in and buy a teleport scroll to the other, teleport there and u can do the main quests there from level one and up. Also, alternate between Klaipeda and Orshas MQ's. Once you reach a level 55 dungeon on one of them and left off on a 53 dungeon on the other, then do the lowest first and continue doing that and you shouldnt have problems leveling up from there.
3. SAVE YOUR EXP CARDS. Dont use them! Sure they give u a flat amount of exp but if your to high a level in a quest, you wont get as much as exp back and you ended up actually loosing out on exp. Look up a Tree of Savior exp graph and you will notice the exp level resets on 46 i believe, so on levels 40-45 where the exp bar is really high, use ur cards to get over that stump so that once ur exp resets and ur in a level 45 dungeons, you will level up faster as well since ur exp bar resest. Plus once you reach the level 50 dungeon, you will jump to like maybe around 60 once u do ur two dungeon runs there. (btw can only run a dungeon twice a day, though not sure if it resets once u unlock another dungeon)
4. If your lagging and your channel is full (all red, especially in town) then switch channels.
5. Get the Cafrisun set that you can farm or buy (prefer to buy since bots and other people farm in the different channels). Its only about 8-10k in market, just buy the lowest costing set and ur good! Its a really good armor set and itll last you till about level 80-100. It can also be equipped at level 15 so thats even better!
6. If you're weighing so much and cant run, it's your SP Potions! They well stack up and is almost useless as a Cleric/Preist/any other support class, drops some points into SPR and you will never run out of Sp because i never do.
7. Finally, its best to look up some guides and see what stats are best to put into for each class, you dont want to screw up like my friend and have to pay to reset and change and change (unless you find a stat reset potion)
Anyways, it is a lengthy review and my first to. It's a really fun game and I hope more people give it a try and dont pass it up like i almost did. Game puts you into role of border inspector for fictional totalitarian republic surrounded by other so called republic. It quite nicely recreates the feeling and atmosphere of this Cold War era. State behaves with its totalitarian authority, immigrants are begging you to let them in.
You are bound by rules how to perform your duty and those rules are changed as story and time progress. So from simple "do you have passport?" it evolves into "do you have papers X Y Z and if needed W?" while you have to check all the data and find all discrepancies. Failing to do so is penalized.
This might sound boring at first, but this puzzle can catch you fast :) It also learns .. or forces you to create a procedure of you own how to procede with data checks if you want to be efficient (which you have to be cause you are payed by "customer" not by a minute and time is limited). And once you find your procedure game throws in another paper or changes previous one and its up to you to adapt.
As the story/days progress, you are also put into many decisions where applicants might not have their papers in order but your Human side tells you to let them in. Or the might have requets regarding their relatives. ("Medicine in your country can save my life, our cant. Please let me in" - Will you? or will you not? .) )
For sure I recommend this for everybody, thats likes to tease their brain :)

This game is not made to be ruled by campaigns and pre laid out story lines, this is a game made so the only limitation to your creations is your imagination.  But as with all games it has a few drawbacks that make the game frustrating to play (I am mostly talking about multiplayer). So I will lay out all the pros and cons and you can decide if it's worth buying, while I think it is worth buying personally.
Pros:
1.) Creativity: This game allows you to build your factory without limiting size or what you can do, it is up to you how far you go in your quest to simply produce more materials to advance further and eventually build the rocket to escape the planet if you want to.
2.) Simple graphics: Few other indie games use simple graphics as well as this game does, although a lot of modern gamers would say that simple graphics is a drawback I believe that if you can make it immersive enough with that simplicity it makes the game better.
3.) Multiplayer GAMEPLAY: I say gameplay in all caps because I do not like the way the multiplayer is set up, I will elaborate on that further in the cons but I want to clarify that although playing this game with friends makes it much better as I believe that multiplayer is an important part of a freebuilding creation game such as this. And if you can manage to get multiplayer working it is extremely fun.
Cons:
1.) Confusing for new players: This game has a tutorial in the campaign but although that explains the mechanics for the beginning the game basically expects you to finish the campaign if you want the rest of the mechanis to be explained to you, and as a new player I was confused and my first few factories were not nearly as efficient as they could have been because I wasn't sure how everything works. Some people may like being thrown into a game but I feel many people may not enjoy this part of the game.
2.) Multiplayer setup: I put multiplayer gameplay as a pro above but how terrible it is to actually get a game in your friends is a huge con. The multiplayer system built into the game didn't work at all for me in fact. Me and my friend had to go download a free program called Evolve online which I highly suggest for people looking to play multiplayer easily in this game as well as many other games.
I understand this is a newer game and I hope to see these cons fixed over time, overall the gameplay is amazing and the freebuild-sandbox feeling is great.

This game made me relive one of the worst periods of my entire life. But it also made me relive one of the best periods of my life.

The friendzone ain't a myth. I played this game religiously on conole, but got a new gaming computer and decided to run through it on a harder difficulty to see if it could scare me like it used to. I spent two hours playing this last night, and here's a summary of how that went:
- Ruined Amanda Ripley's posture for life, because I basically never once got her up out of crouch.
- Jumped and yelped at my own room noises, like a water bottle crackling or my bed creaking.
- Probably decimated my eyesight and hearing, because I pushed the screen up to my retinas and maxed out the volume to make sure I didn't f**king die horribly.
- Spent waaaaay too long hiding under a desk or in a locker, convinced that the second I left I would f**king die horribly.
This went on for two hours before the ominous music, sparking lights and Alien-noises in the distance gave me PTSD and forced me to go to bed and try and find solace in the oblivion of unconsciounsness. On a serious note, this is by far and away the best horror game I've ever played, and I've played a few; you're not a super-soldier, you're not a mega-warrior, you're not a psychic goddess - you're a person. A badass, but ultimately mortal, person, and that feeling of frailty in the face of overwhelming, Alien-inspired terror is utterly unique. Seriously, there is no game made that is like this one; sure, Dead Space might come close, but it really doesn't. Nothing does. Nothing can drop your stomach, pump your heart and shrink your balls (or your ovaries) like this game does. It's my favorite horror game of all time.

This game is amazing! The graphics are really good, and if your computer can't handle it on normal, you can just bring them down to your liking. The only thing I dislike about this game, is how sometimes you cannot have a friend playing with you in certain areas. Which is terrifying! But it's fun to be scared sometimes.. ;) This game is also realllllly hard sometimes as well, but if you have a friend who participates in the game with you regularly, you should be okay. You may have to try multiple times even with a friend, but it is easier if someone is with you. I've had multiple instances where I had my friend play with me, and we still had a ton of trouble and died a lot. So, just because you have someone with you doesn't mean you WILL be okay, it just means that maybe, and I mean MAYBE, you can make it through a bit further. Just remember to keep going and PRAISE THE SUN! :) I would recommend this game to anyone, so long as you can control your anger/rage. This is because you will die. A lot. I also love how the game has puzzles, and you learn from your mistakes. This game is open world, which is EVEN better! I LOVE open world! You can pretty much go anywhere in this game. Including falling off the edge if you aren't paying attention. And, if you are having trouble being invaded, you can always play offline. I'm glad we have that choice as well. 10 out of 10 for this game. OH, and one more thing, when I first started playing the game, the controls were a absolute pain for me to learn. I've never had a game with these controls before, but have no fear! If you are having this issue you can change the controls to your liking, or leave it as it is, learn it, and over time you will get used to it.

Broforce is, in its essence, a member of the 2D platforms that a standard gamer absolutely needs to play. The games difficult. I wouldn't say it's among the hardest, but you'll certainly hit a spike sooner or later. The presentation is gorgeous, but maybe thats because pixel art is my thing. Gameplay itself is the games high point. Enemy placement is well thought out, but with one flaw: The standard enemies are super dumb. I mean, really dumb. They'll shoot about 25 shots a minute, essentially turning them into bullet pillows. It's not until you meet the other enemies that you realize what makes the gameplay so tense. The other two main enemies are as follows: a huge machine gunner who can take you out with ONE of the hundreds of bullets that fire from his gun, and a suicide bomber, which is relatively self explanatory.
I strongly recommend this game. It's so much fun, and its a pure gem in the genre its from. If you're questioning whether this games worth it or not, I have good news for you! On steam, there's a side game for Broforce, called the expendabros. I highly recommend playing it to be sure you like the physics of the game, and its completely free.

Have you read "The Mysterious Island" by Jules Verne? Have you ever imagined yourself in the place of brave travelers? Have you ever thought what would you do in their shoes to survive? I experienced this novel with its characters several times, and with Cyrus Smith improves the lives of unwitting colonists and built a new civilization away from the rest of the world. Now imagine that you are in a similar situation, and you can independently use their skills and abilities to help yourself out with the "mysterious island". How? Modern computer games allow you to check it for yourself. I accidentally found on the Internet site of the game “Factorio”. Imagine the distant future. You are the pilot of a spaceship that crashed on a distant planet. And you have to try to leave this planet from scratch building a mining and processing industries, creating assembly lines and research centers and in the end build a spaceship. But all is not as easy as it seems. The Resources are few, and the planet is inhabited and its inhabitants, dissatisfied with pollution caused by your production, begin to attack you and you need to defend yourself from their attacks.
The idea of ​​this game and the opportunity to relive childhood memories fascinated me and I enthusiastically cast aside all my current affairs and began to play! Although at first glance the game is not boring, but in the game there are situations related to the routine "work" and a manifested monotony. In the early stages this “dig-extractive-operation-researching” process turns into the “dig-extraction-system-researching” process but for the next level of development of science and technology. Stone furnace is replaced by the steel furnace and electric technology as the study and improvement of science, steam generators are replaced with solar panels on the coal is replaced with a crude oil and other forms of energy. But in the end you achieve the ultimate goal!
In general, the game has caused pleasant emotions in me and I feel it will remain in my library of games for a long time
